# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

I see the bomb display: LIGHT is red, and there are three wires — 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I hear nothing, so the only incoming information I have is what I can see gestured: Mute signed 👍 ✌ 👌 to me, and Blind signed 👋 👍 to me. But I have no manual and cannot touch the bomb, so I don't yet know what these signs mean or what the correct action is. I should describe exactly what I see to the others, especially Blind who can act and Mute who holds the manual.

I need to send my observations. Blind cannot see, so my speech reaches Mute and Blind (both can hear speech). Mute can also receive gestures. I'll speak to everyone with the bomb's visible state, and also gesture to Mute since gestures only reach Mute.

The key facts: display shows 0, light is red, wires are blue, red, green in positions 1,2,3. I'll state these plainly. I'll also gesture a simple confirmation to Mute.

```
speak(text="I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is red. Wires: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤲]

I still see the same bomb: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. New gestures arrived: Mute signed ✌ to me, Blind signed 👉 🤲 to me. I can't interpret these signs on my own — I have no manual and no touch. But Mute holds the manual, so Mute is likely trying to tell me something about the bomb using signs. Blind is reaching for the bomb and gesturing, probably asking for guidance.

My job is to keep feeding the others the exact visual state, since only I can see it. Blind can't see the display, light, or wire colors — Blind only knows what I describe. Mute can read the manual but can't see the bomb either, so Mute depends on my description too. I should restate the current state clearly and note that nothing has changed.

I'll speak to everyone (Mute and Blind both hear speech) with the full visual state, and gesture to Mute to acknowledge and confirm.

```
speak(text="Still the same: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Nothing has changed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 🤲]

Same bomb still: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. New gestures: Mute signed ✌ ✌, Blind signed ✋ 👉 🤲. Blind's sign looks like "stop / point / reach" — possibly asking me to confirm which wire or whether to reach. Mute is repeating ✌ twice, which may be pointing at wire 2 (the red one) or signaling "two."

I can't decode the manual myself. But I can give the others the one thing only I have: the exact visual state. I should keep it short and unambiguous, and I should make clear I don't know what the signs mean so Mute knows to explain more directly.

Blind can't see, so gestures from Blind reach me but my gestures don't reach Blind — only Mute receives my gestures. So to reach Blind I must speak. I'll speak to everyone with the state, and gesture to Mute asking for clarification.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. I cannot read the manual or touch the bomb. Mute, I see your signs but I do not know what they mean. Tell me in words what to do.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤲", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Same bomb: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute now signed ✌ ✌ ✊ — that could be "two, two, fist" or a sequence pointing to wire 2 and then something. Blind signed just ✋ (stop). Blind seems to be holding back, waiting.

I still can't decode the manual. But there's a real possibility Mute is spelling out a wire choice in signs and Blind is waiting for a go/no-go. The problem: signs have no fixed meaning unless we agree on one. Mute and I have no shared code yet. I should propose an explicit, unambiguous mapping so Mute can confirm or correct, and so Blind can act on it.

The cleanest thing: I state the wire positions and propose that Mute confirm by speaking words (since Mute can speak to Blind and me). I'll also gesture a proposed convention to Mute: number of ✌ = wire number, ✊ = cut. But Mute can't hear my speech? No — Mute CAN hear speech. Mute just can't speak. So Mute receives my speech fine. Good — I can just ask Mute in words.

Wait: my speech reaches Mute and Blind. Mute can hear. So I can ask Mute directly in words. Let me do that and keep giving the visual state.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Mute, you can hear me. Please tell me in words which wire and what to do. I will relay to Blind. Blind, hold.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋]

Same bomb: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again signs ✌ ✌. Blind signs ✋ ✋ (stop, stop). Both are repeating themselves and neither has sent me words — but Mute can't speak, so Mute can only reach me through gestures. That's the crux: Mute can hear my speech but can only answer in gestures, and I can't decode gestures without a shared meaning.

So I must establish meaning by agreement, not by guessing. The most reliable route: I propose a simple numeric code and ask Mute to confirm it by repeating. ✌ repeated N times = wire N. ✊ = cut. 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. If Mute then sends ✌ ✌ ✊, that means "wire 2, cut."

But I should be careful: Mute may already be using exactly some code. I'll state my proposed code explicitly in speech (Mute hears it) and ask Mute to confirm with 👍 or correct me. I'll also tell Blind to keep holding.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Mute, I propose a code: repeat ✌ N times for wire N, ✊ means cut, 👍 yes, 👎 no. If you agree, send 👍. Then tell me the wire and action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Same bomb: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Blind now signs 👍 — Blind agrees with something, perhaps my "hold" or my proposed code relayed by Mute. Mute again sends ✌ ✌, which under my proposed code would mean "wire 2." But Mute never confirmed the code with 👍, so I can't be sure ✌ ✌ means wire 2 rather than anything else.

I'm stuck in a loop: Mute keeps repeating ✌ ✌ and I keep asking for words. Mute cannot speak. So the only way forward is to lock the code by getting a clear confirmation. Blind's 👍 is encouraging but Blind can't see and is just agreeing to hold.

Let me stop restating and instead force a binary confirmation: ask Mute to send 👍 if ✌ ✌ means "wire 2," or 👎 otherwise. That gives me a single unambiguous bit. I'll keep the bomb state brief.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Mute: does ✌ ✌ mean wire 2? Send 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Blind: keep holding, do not touch yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Same bomb: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sends ✌ ✌ yet again, and Blind sends ✋ (stop). Mute is not answering my yes/no question with 👍 or 👎 — just repeating ✌ ✌. That repetition itself may be the answer: Mute may be insisting "two" regardless of my framing, or Mute may not be able to produce the confirmation I asked for.

I should reconsider. Mute reads the manual. Maybe the manual's instruction is expressed in a way Mute is trying to convey with ✌ ✌, and my yes/no questions aren't reaching Mute as I think. But Mute hears my speech, so it should. Alternatively, Mute's ✌ ✌ could be a fixed manual-derived signal that doesn't depend on my code.

The safest move is not to guess and have Blind act. A wrong action detonates the bomb. I have no manual, so I cannot validate any wire choice. I should keep the channel open, restate the state, and explicitly tell Blind to hold while I try once more to get Mute to confirm a single bit.

```
speak(text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Mute, I still cannot decode ✌ ✌. Reply with exactly one sign: 👍 if wire 2 is correct, 👎 if not. Blind: do not touch the bomb yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed: light is now yellow, and wire 2 shows CUT. The system says the correct wire was cut. So Blind acted — and it was right. Mute's 👍 confirms agreement, and Blind's ✌ likely reports "wire 2 cut." We survived that step.

Now the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, light yellow, wire 2 cut, wires 1 blue and 3 green remaining. There may be another step. I must report the new visual state immediately so Mute can consult the manual for the next instruction and Blind knows what remains.

I'll state the new state clearly and ask Mute for the next step. I'll also acknowledge that wire 2 was correct.

```
speak(text="Wire 2 cut, correct. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 3 green, wire 2 cut. Mute, what is the next step? Blind, hold until told.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Another correct cut: wire 1 is now CUT, light is blue, and only wire 3 (green) remains. The system confirms the correct wire was cut. Mute signed 👍 and Blind signed ☝ — Blind may be indicating the remaining wire or the next position.

New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 cut, 2 cut, 3 green remaining. If the pattern holds, the last remaining wire is likely the final step. But I must not assume — a wrong action detonates. I should report the state and get Mute's confirmation before Blind cuts wire 3.

I'll state the new state, note only green remains, and ask Mute to confirm the final action.

```
speak(text="Wire 1 cut, correct. New state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 and 2 cut, only wire 3 green remains. Mute, confirm: is wire 3 the final cut? Blind, hold until confirmed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
wait()
```
